definitions.explanation: A polite, euphemistic way to say someone has died. More respectful than 死ぬ.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{去年|きょねん}{亡|な}くなった。
examples.english: My grandfather passed away last year.

examples.japanese: {事故|じこ}で{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}が{亡|な}くなった。
examples.english: Many people died in the accident.

examples.japanese: お{母様|かあさま}が{亡|な}くなられたそうですね。
examples.english: I heard your mother passed away.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive). Pattern: Xが{亡|な}くなる (X passes away).

{亡|な}くなる is the polite/euphemistic word for dying.

USAGE:
- More polite than {死|し}ぬ
- Used when referring to someone's death respectfully
- Common in news reports and formal situations
- Often used when expressing condolences

HONORIFIC FORMS:
- {亡|な}くなられる (honorific)
- お{亡|な}くなりになる (more honorific)

HOMOPHONE:
- {無|な}くなる (to disappear, to run out) - different kanji

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {亡|な}くなる: to pass away (polite)
- {死|し}ぬ: to die (direct, can be harsh)
- {逝|い}く: to pass (literary)
